answer: An agent market requires each seller identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Agents offering umber pigment, meadow surveys, or voyage planning face the same rule: one active job per bonded identity. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000 rather than producing free bidding capacity. Sybils remain possible, but each extra identity buys only one slot and imposes a month of capital lockup on its operator.
